name: Fried Carrot Cake
description: Cubes of steamed radish cake wok-fried in dark sweet sauce with egg, garlic and preserved radish. The edges crisp and caramelise while the centre stays custardy soft, delivering smoky wok hei in every savoury bite.
stall: He Zhong Carrot Cake, Maxwell Food Centre

name: Chicken Chop
description: A juicy grilled chicken leg glazed in peppery brown sauce, served hawker-western style with crinkle-cut fries, baked beans and coleslaw. Comforting, hearty and generous, it is a nostalgic plate loved since school canteen days.
stall: Western Barbeque, Maxwell Food Centre

name: Ondeh Ondeh
description: Chewy pandan-scented glutinous rice balls rolled in fresh grated coconut, hiding molten gula melaka that bursts sweetly on the first bite. A beloved kueh that pairs perfectly with afternoon tea or kopi.
stall: Nyonya Kueh House, Maxwell Food Centre

name: Claypot Rice
description: Rice cooked over charcoal in a blackened claypot with chicken, salted fish, lap cheong and dark soy drizzle. The prized crust at the bottom crackles with smoky caramel notes, worth the thirty-minute wait.
stall: Heng Ji Claypot Rice, Chinatown Complex Food Centre

name: Sliced Fish Bee Hoon
description: Fresh batang fish slices poached in a milky, wok-charred broth with rice vermicelli, tomato, ginger and a splash of evaporated milk. Clean, sweet and restorative, it is the lunch Singaporeans crave on rainy days.
stall: Tong Kee Fish Soup, Chinatown Complex Food Centre

name: Char Siew Rice
description: 叉烧肥瘦均匀，蜜汁烤得焦香，边缘微微炭化带着烟熏甜味。斩件铺在热腾腾的白饭上，淋上甜咸交织的酱汁，再配一碗清汤和几片黄瓜，是牛车水街坊几十年来最熟悉的午餐滋味。
stall: Foong Kee Roasted Delights, Chinatown Complex Food Centre

name: Chee Cheong Fun
description: Silky steamed rice rolls draped in sweet dark sauce, sesame oil and a scatter of toasted sesame seeds. Slippery, delicate and lightly nutty, it is a quick, satisfying breakfast that slides down easily.
stall: Freshly Made Chee Cheong Fun, Chinatown Complex Food Centre

name: Luo Han Guo Drink
description: Monk fruit brewed with dried longan and chrysanthemum into a dark amber infusion, naturally sweet with herbal depth. Chilled over ice, it cools the body after fiery chilli-laden hawker feasts.
stall: Chinatown Herbal Tea Stall, Chinatown Complex Food Centre

name: Chwee Kueh
description: 米浆蒸成的水粿嫩滑如布丁，中间微微凹陷，盛满咸香回甘的菜脯粒，油润喷香。淋一点手工辣椒酱，趁热一口一个，配上一杯热咖啡，是中峇鲁市场最经典的传统早餐风景。
stall: Jian Bo Shui Kueh, Tiong Bahru Market

name: Lor Mee
description: Thick yellow noodles bathed in a glossy, starchy braising gravy laced with five spice, vinegar, garlic and chilli. Topped with crispy fish nuggets, braised egg and pork belly, it is sticky, tangy comfort in a bowl.
stall: Tiong Bahru Lor Mee, Tiong Bahru Market

name: Steamed Pau
description: Pillowy handmade buns steamed to a soft cloud, filled with sweet-savoury braised pork, chicken with egg, or smooth lotus paste. Fluffy, warm and portable, they are a classic teatime and breakfast staple.
stall: Tiong Bahru Pau & Snacks, Tiong Bahru Market

name: Soya Beancurd
description: Impossibly smooth soybean pudding that wobbles at the touch of a spoon, served warm or chilled with clear sugar syrup. Light, silky and gently sweet, it is the classic finish to a hawker meal.
stall: Teck Seng Soya Bean, Tiong Bahru Market

name: You Tiao
description: Golden dough fritters fried till airy and crackly, eaten plain, dunked into hot soybean milk, or dipped in fragrant bak kwa-sweet sauces. Crunchy outside, chewy within, an old-school breakfast indulgence.
stall: Traditional You Tiao Stall, Tiong Bahru Market

name: Rojak
description: A boisterous salad of pineapple, cucumber, turnip, you tiao and blanched cuttlefish tossed in pungent prawn paste sauce with lime, chilli and crushed peanuts. Sweet, funky, crunchy and utterly addictive.
stall: Toa Payoh Rojak (Old Airport Branch), Old Airport Road Food Centre

name: Beef Hor Fun
description: Wide rice noodles seared over ferocious flame until smoky, then smothered in silky egg gravy with tender marinated beef slices. The interplay of charred noodles and velvety sauce defines classic zi char mastery.
stall: Freshly Fried Hor Fun, Old Airport Road Food Centre

name: Kway Chap
description: 滑溜的宽粿条浸在深色药材卤汁里，配上卤豆干、卤蛋、猪肠、五花肉和菜尾。卤香浓郁回甘，猪肠处理得干净软糯，入口即化，蘸上蒜蓉辣椒醋更是一绝，是老加东人周末的心头好。
stall: Blanco Court Kway Chap, Old Airport Road Food Centre

name: Ice Kacang
description: A glistening mountain of shaved ice drenched in rose syrup, gula melaka and creamy evaporated milk, hiding red beans, sweet corn, attap chee and grass jelly beneath. The ultimate tropical cooldown on a sweltering afternoon.
stall: Old Airport Cool Desserts, Old Airport Road Food Centre

name: Cuttlefish Kangkong
description: Blanched water spinach and springy cuttlefish dressed generously with sweet dark shrimp sauce, fiery chilli and a snowfall of crushed peanuts. Crunchy, chewy and savoury-sweet, an old-school Katong favourite.
stall: Ah Lam Cuttlefish Kangkong, Old Airport Road Food Centre

name: Vadai
description: உளுந்து மாவில் இஞ்சி, பச்சை மிளகாய், கறிவேப்பிலை சேர்த்து மொறுமொறுப்பாகப் பொரித்த வடை. வெளியே கருகருவென்றும் உள்ளே மென்மையாகவும் இருக்கும். மாலை நேரத் தேநீருடன் சூடாகச் சாப்பிட மிக அருமையான தெக்கா சந்தை சிற்றுண்டி.
stall: Tekka Vadai Corner, Tekka Centre

name: Tandoori Chicken with Naan
description: Yoghurt-and-spice marinated chicken charred in a blistering clay oven until smoky and crimson, served with pillowy garlic naan and cooling mint chutney. The juicy meat pulls cleanly off the bone.
stall: Delhi Tandoor House, Tekka Centre

name: Mutton Kurma with Rice
description: Tender mutton simmered in a mild, nutty gravy of cashew, yoghurt, cardamom and coriander, ladled over fluffy basmati with pickled onions. Rich yet gentle, perfect for those who love aroma over heat.
stall: Bismillah Curry House, Tekka Centre

name: Putu Mayam
description: மெல்லிய நூல்கள் போன்ற ஆவியில் வேகவைத்த புட்டு மயம், துருவிய தேங்காயும் சிவப்பு சர்க்கரையும் தூவிப் பரிமாறப்படுகிறது. மென்மையான, லேசான இனிப்பு; காலை உணவுக்கும் தேநீர் நேரத்துக்கும் மிகவும் ஏற்ற பாரம்பரிய உணவு.
stall: Heritage Putu Mayam, Tekka Centre

name: Mango Lassi
description: Ripe mango blended with thick homemade yoghurt into a frothy, tangy-sweet drink, finished with a whisper of cardamom. Cold, creamy and luscious, it tames even the most fiery curry lunch.
stall: Tekka Juice & Lassi Bar, Tekka Centre

name: Idli with Sambar
description: Feather-light steamed rice-and-lentil cakes served with tangy sambar and fresh coconut chutney. Soft, spongy and gently sour from overnight fermentation, this South Indian breakfast is wholesome, comforting and naturally vegetarian.
stall: Madras Woodlands Corner, Little India Arcade

name: Samosa
description: Crisp triangular pastry parcels packed with spiced potato, green peas and cumin, fried to a deep golden crunch. Eaten hot with tamarind chutney, they are the quintessential teatime bite along Serangoon Road.
stall: Ameen Samosa Stall, Little India Arcade

name: Indian Rojak
description: A pick-and-mix platter of crispy fritters, boiled egg, potato, prawn cakes and firm tofu, refried to order and dunked in a sweet-spicy orange peanut gravy. Crunchy, messy and gloriously indulgent.
stall: Hussain Indian Rojak, Buffalo Road Stalls

name: Falooda
description: A tall rose-pink parfait layering vermicelli strands, basil seeds, jelly, ice cream and chilled milk. Floral, creamy and playfully textured, this Indian-Muslim dessert drink is a celebration in a glass.
stall: Royal Falooda House, Little India Arcade

name: Masala Chai
description: Strong black tea boiled with milk, ginger, cardamom and cloves, then pulled between jugs until frothy. Warming, aromatic and lightly sweet, it is the heartbeat of every conversation along Serangoon Road.
stall: Chennai Tea Stall, Buffalo Road Stalls

name: Nasi Padang with Beef Rendang
description: Daging lembu direneh berjam-jam dengan rempah kampung, serai, lengkuas dan cili kering hingga empuk dan kuahnya pekat berkilat. Dihidangkan dengan nasi putih panas, sayur lodeh dan sambal belacan, kegemaran pengunjung Geylang Serai terutama menjelang hari raya.
stall: Warong Haji Sarbini, Geylang Serai Market

name: Goreng Pisang
description: Pisang raja disaluti tepung istimewa lalu digoreng hingga keemasan dan rangup. Bahagian luar garing berderak, isinya manis, lembut dan wangi. Paling sedap dinikmati panas-panas bersama secawan teh pada waktu petang di Geylang Serai.
stall: Pisang Goreng Mak Timah, Geylang Serai Market

name: Mee Siam
description: Thin rice vermicelli in a tangy-sweet spiced gravy brightened with tamarind and fermented bean, crowned with boiled egg, tau pok, chives and a squeeze of calamansi. Zesty, light and moreish at breakfast.
stall: Hajjah Mona Mee Siam, Geylang Serai Market

name: Putu Piring
description: Delicate steamed rice-flour cakes concealing molten gula melaka hearts, pressed flat and served on fresh grated coconut with pandan. Each warm, crumbly bite melts into smoky palm-sugar sweetness.
stall: Traditional Haig Road Putu Piring, Geylang Serai Market

name: Air Bandung
description: Rose syrup swirled into chilled evaporated milk for a blush-pink drink that is floral, creamy and nostalgically sweet. A staple at Malay weddings and the perfect partner to spicy market fare.
stall: Geylang Serai Air Corner, Geylang Serai Market

name: Har Cheong Gai
description: Chicken mid-wings marinated in pungent fermented prawn paste, then deep-fried to a shatteringly crisp, savoury-funky crust. A beloved zi char classic best eaten scorching hot with a cold beer.
stall: Two Chefs Eating Place, Commonwealth Crescent Market

name: Fishball Noodles
description: Springy mee pok tossed in chilli, vinegar and lard, paired with bouncy handmade fishballs in a clear, peppery broth on the side. Simple, honest Teochew flavours that keep queues forming daily.
stall: Teochew Fishball Noodle King, Amoy Street Food Centre

name: Salted Egg Chicken Rice Bowl
description: Crispy chicken chunks lacquered in a golden salted egg yolk sauce with curry leaves and chilli padi, piled over pearl rice with a molten onsen egg. Rich, buttery, savoury and dangerously addictive.
stall: Golden Yolk Bowls, Amoy Street Food Centre

name: Kopi O
description: Robusta beans roasted with sugar and margarine, sock-brewed the traditional way into a bold, bittersweet black coffee. Thick, smoky and aromatic, it fuels the CBD crowd from dawn till lunch.
stall: Nanyang Kopi Stall, Amoy Street Food Centre

name: Thunder Tea Rice
description: A Hakka bowl of brown rice topped with chopped greens, tofu, peanuts and preserved radish, served with a vivid emerald broth of ground tea, basil and mint. Herbaceous, nutty and virtuously nourishing.
stall: Hakka Lei Cha House, Amoy Street Food Centre

name: Sup Kambing
description: Indian-Muslim mutton soup simmered for hours with a heady blend of spices, fresh herbs and fried shallots, served with torn baguette for dunking. Peppery, warming and deeply restorative on a late night.
stall: Bahrakath Mutton Soup, Lau Pa Sat

name: Yang Chow Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice tossed in a searing wok with prawns, char siew, egg and spring onion until every grain is loose, fragrant and kissed with smoke. A zi char benchmark done with old-school finesse.
stall: Wok Master Fried Rice, Lau Pa Sat

name: Roast Duck Rice
description: Cantonese-style duck roasted until the skin is lacquered mahogany and crisp, the meat succulent beneath. Served over fragrant rice with plum-tinged drippings, braised egg and cucumber for a hearty city lunch.
stall: Canton Roast Duck, Lau Pa Sat

name: Milo Dinosaur
description: Iced malted chocolate drink buried under a generous avalanche of undissolved Milo powder. Cold, creamy and outrageously chocolatey, this uniquely Singaporean invention delights kids and fuels late-night supper crews alike.
stall: Lau Pa Sat Drinks Junction, Lau Pa Sat

name: BBQ Chicken Wings
description: Wings marinated overnight then grilled over charcoal until the skin blisters, crisps and drips with smoky-sweet juices. Squeeze over calamansi, dip in garlic chilli, and order another round immediately.
stall: Huat Huat BBQ Chicken Wings, Newton Food Centre

name: Cereal Prawns
description: Jumbo prawns flash-fried then tumbled through buttery Nestum cereal, curry leaves and chilli padi. The crunchy, fragrant flakes cling to sweet, snappy prawn flesh in this beloved zi char showstopper.
stall: Newton Seafood Delight, Newton Food Centre

name: Sambal Kangkong
description: Water spinach flash-fried on roaring heat with pungent belacan sambal until just wilted and smoky. Spicy, savoury and crunchy-stemmed, it is the essential green companion to any zi char seafood spread.
stall: Newton Seafood Delight, Newton Food Centre

name: Fresh Lime Juice
description: Small calamansi limes squeezed to order over ice with a touch of sour plum, balancing bright citrus zing with salty-sweet depth. The sharpest, most refreshing antidote to chilli-heavy feasting.
stall: Newton Fresh Juice Stall, Newton Food Centre

name: BBQ Sambal Sotong
description: Whole squid slathered in fiery house-pounded sambal, wrapped and grilled over glowing coals by the beach. Smoky, spicy and tender with a gentle chew, best enjoyed with sea breeze and cold drinks.
stall: Lagoon BBQ Seafood, East Coast Lagoon Food Village

name: Fish and Chips
description: Dory fillet in a light, crackly golden batter with thick-cut fries, tartare sauce and a lemon wedge. Fried to order by the seaside, it is breezy holiday food without the airfare.
stall: Seaside Western Grill, East Coast Lagoon Food Village

name: Seafood Hor Fun
description: Charred flat rice noodles drowned in a glossy seafood gravy brimming with prawns, squid and fish slices. The smoky noodles soak up the sweet, eggy sauce for a satisfying beachside dinner.
stall: Lagoon Wok & Fire, East Coast Lagoon Food Village

name: Coconut Shake
description: Young coconut flesh and juice blended with vanilla ice cream into a frosty, tropical slush, topped with a creamy scoop. Nutty, fragrant and ice-cold, it is pure beach-day bliss in a cup.
stall: Coco Loco Shakes, East Coast Lagoon Food Village

name: Oyster Omelette
description: Plump briny oysters folded into a crisp-edged egg and starch omelette, fried in lard until lacy and golden, then hit with garlicky chilli-vinegar sauce. Gooey, crunchy and savoury all at once.
stall: Ah Hock Fried Oyster, Chomp Chomp Food Centre

name: White Carrot Cake
description: Radish cake fried the pale way with copious egg, fish sauce and preserved radish, so the surface crisps golden while the inside stays soft and steamy. Lighter than the dark version, equally addictive.
stall: Chomp Chomp Carrot Cake, Chomp Chomp Food Centre

name: Sambal Lala
description: Sweet clams tossed in a bubbling wok of sambal, ginger and basil until their shells gape open and soak up the fiery gravy. Messy, spicy, finger-licking supper food made for sharing.
stall: Serangoon Zi Char Seafood, Chomp Chomp Food Centre

name: Sugarcane with Lemon
description: Sugarcane stalks crushed fresh through the press, sharpened with a squeeze of lemon and served in a towering icy mug. Grassy-sweet, tart and endlessly gulpable beside smoky barbecue plates.
stall: Chomp Chomp Sugarcane Specialist, Chomp Chomp Food Centre

name: Braised Duck Rice
description: 老卤慢炖的鸭肉软嫩入味，斩件后淋上浓稠发亮的卤汁，配白饭或香浓芋头饭。附上卤蛋、豆干和花生，再来一碟酸菜和姜蓉辣椒解腻，是传统潮州人从小吃到大的味道。
stall: Ghim Moh Teochew Braised Duck, Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre

name: Soon Kueh
description: Translucent chewy rice-flour skins wrapped around juicy bamboo shoot, turnip and dried shrimp filling, steamed then brushed with shallot oil. Dip in dark sweet sauce and chilli for a Teochew teatime classic.
stall: Ghim Moh Traditional Kueh, Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre

name: Curry Chicken Noodles
description: Thick rice noodles and yellow mee swimming in a rich, spice-laden curry gravy with tender chicken, tau pok and potato. The lush, fragrant broth carries gentle heat and a creamy coconut finish.
stall: Ghim Moh Curry Chicken Mee, Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre

name: Epok Epok
description: Hand-crimped pastry half-moons fried till blistered and crisp, filled with spiced potato, curried chicken or sardine with a wedge of egg. A humble Malay snack that disappears by mid-morning.
stall: Epok Epok Asli, Ghim Moh Market & Food Centre

name: Yong Tau Foo
description: Pick your own tofu, chilli, bittergourd and mushroom pieces stuffed with springy fish paste, served in a clear anchovy-sweet broth or tossed dry with sweet bean sauce. Fresh, customisable and light.
stall: Hakka Yong Tau Foo, Ang Mo Kio 724 Market

name: Png Kueh
description: Pink-skinned Teochew kueh shaped like a peach, packed with savoury glutinous rice, dried shrimp, mushroom and peanuts. Steamed soft or pan-fried till crisp, it is nostalgic morning-market fare.
stall: Traditional Teochew Kueh Stall, Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre

name: Soya Bean Milk
description: Soybeans ground and boiled fresh each dawn into a smooth, gently sweet milk served hot or over ice. Clean, nutty and comforting, it pairs naturally with you tiao at breakfast.
stall: Fresh Soya Bean Stall, Mayflower Market & Food Centre

name: Hakka Abacus Seeds
description: Chewy yam and tapioca discs shaped like abacus beads, stir-fried with minced pork, dried shrimp, mushrooms and black fungus. Earthy, springy and savoury, a treasured Hakka dish rarely found in hawker centres.
stall: Hakka Heritage Delights, Ang Mo Kio 724 Market

name: Braised Duck Noodles
description: Flat rice noodles slicked with dark herbal braising sauce and starchy gravy, layered with slices of tender braised duck and a sprinkle of fried shallots. Robust, aromatic Teochew comfort for lunch crowds.
stall: Toa Payoh Duck Noodle House, Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market

name: Ngoh Hiang
description: Beancurd skin rolls stuffed with seasoned minced pork, prawn and water chestnut, deep-fried till crackly and served with sweet flour sauce and chilli. Crunchy, juicy party food from Hokkien kitchens.
stall: Old School Ngoh Hiang, Kim Keat Palm Market

name: Tang Yuan
description: Chewy glutinous rice balls filled with molten black sesame or crushed peanut, floating in warm ginger-infused sweet soup. Soothing and fragrant, traditionally eaten during winter solstice but craved year-round.
stall: Sweet Reunion Desserts, Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market

name: Kopi Gu You
description: Traditional sock-pulled kopi crowned with a melting knob of butter that slicks the strong, sweet brew with silky richness. An old Hainanese indulgence that still charms uncles and hipsters alike.
stall: Heritage Kopi Stall, Kim Keat Palm Market

name: Ang Ku Kueh
description: Glossy crimson tortoise-shaped kueh with a chewy glutinous skin over sweet mung bean or peanut filling, pressed on a banana-scented base. Auspicious, sticky and subtly sweet, a birthday and festival essential.
stall: Ji Xiang Confectionery Stall, Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market

name: Hainanese Beef Noodles
description: Slippery kway teow under a thick, glistening beef gravy with tender slices, tripe and tendon, finished with salted vegetables and ground peanuts. Deep, beefy and tangy, an heirloom Hainanese recipe.
stall: Whampoa Beef Noodle Specialist, Whampoa Drive Makan Place

name: Popiah
description: Paper-thin handmade skins wrapped around sweet stewed turnip, prawns, egg, peanuts and crisp lettuce, painted with sweet flour sauce and garlic. Soft, juicy and crunchy in a single neat roll.
stall: Ann Chin Handmade Popiah, Whampoa Drive Makan Place

name: Orh Nee
description: Velvety Teochew yam paste enriched with shallot oil, crowned with sweet pumpkin cubes and ginkgo nuts. Served warm, it is smooth, earthy and decadently sweet, a banquet dessert gone hawker.
stall: Teochew Dessert House, Whampoa Drive Makan Place

name: Teh C Peng
description: Strong-brewed black tea swirled with evaporated milk and sugar syrup over a tall glass of ice. Smoother and less cloying than condensed-milk teh, it is the everyday cooler of coffeeshop regulars.
stall: Whampoa Kopi & Teh Stall, Whampoa Drive Makan Place

name: Lontong
description: Compressed rice cakes soaked in a turmeric-golden vegetable gravy with cabbage, long beans, tofu and tempeh, topped with boiled egg and spicy sambal. Mellow, creamy and warming, a hearty Malay breakfast.
stall: Warong Kampung Lontong, Ci Yuan Hawker Centre

name: Nasi Goreng Kampung
description: Smoky village-style fried rice tossed with ikan bilis, egg and a fiery belacan-chilli pounding, served with crispy fried chicken wing and cucumber. Rustic, spicy and satisfying any time of day.
stall: Selera Kampung, Ci Yuan Hawker Centre

name: Ayam Buah Keluak
description: Chicken braised in a dark, tangy tamarind gravy with buah keluak nuts whose inky flesh tastes of earth, truffle and bittersweet chocolate. A laborious Peranakan heirloom dish, rarely seen at hawker prices.
stall: Nyonya Heritage Kitchen, Hougang 105 Hainanese Village Centre

name: Grass Jelly Soya Drink
description: Chilled soybean milk poured over ribbons of dark grass jelly, playfully nicknamed for its black-and-white swirl. Silky, herbal and lightly sweet, it is a cheeky thirst-quencher after a spicy meal.
stall: Hougang Soya & Jelly Bar, Ci Yuan Hawker Centre

name: Ayam Penyet
description: Fried chicken leg smashed to loosen its juicy flesh, served with rice, crunchy batter crumbs, fried tofu, tempeh and a devastating pounded sambal. Fragrant, fiery Indonesian-Malay comfort on a plate.
stall: Ayam Penyet Ibu Ros, Boon Lay Place Food Village

name: Roti John
description: A split baguette griddled facedown into a sizzling layer of minced mutton, egg and onion, then squiggled with chilli and mayonnaise. Crispy, eggy and indulgent, a Malay night-market icon.
stall: Roti John Warisan, Boon Lay Place Food Village

name: Cheng Tng
description: A clear, gently sweet dessert broth of longan, barley, gingko, white fungus, sago and candied melon, served hot or iced. Light and nourishing, it is grandma's remedy for heaty days.
stall: Four Seasons Cheng Tng, Jurong West 505 Market

name: Yuan Yang
description: Half kopi, half teh, stirred into one bracing, malty-bitter brew with condensed milk — the indecisive drinker's kopitiam classic. Order it peng over ice for maximum refreshment.
stall: Boon Lay Traditional Kopi, Boon Lay Place Food Village

name: Soy Sauce Chicken Rice
description: Chicken poached in a master stock of premium soy, rock sugar and spices until burnished and silky, served over fragrant rice with drippings. Glossy, tender and savoury-sweet in every bite.
stall: Golden Soy Chicken, Clementi 448 Market & Food Centre

name: Kueh Tutu
description: Dainty steamed rice-flour cakes moulded in tiny cups, filled with ground peanut or orange-hued grated coconut, served on pandan. Warm, fluffy and fleetingly soft, a vanishing street snack of old Singapore.
stall: Traditional Tutu Kueh, Clementi 448 Market & Food Centre

name: Tahu Goreng
description: Golden fried tofu quartered over crisp bean sprouts and cucumber, drowned in a thick, spicy-sweet peanut sauce. Warm, nutty and gently fiery, this Malay classic proves humble tofu can be glorious.
stall: Warong Pak Salleh, Clementi 448 Market & Food Centre

name: Soursop Juice
description: Creamy-white soursop pulp blended with ice into a tangy, fragrant slush with tropical custard-apple notes. Refreshingly tart and naturally sweet, it is an underrated gem among hawker juice stalls.
stall: Clementi Fresh Fruit Juices, Clementi 448 Market & Food Centre

name: Hainanese Curry Rice
description: A gloriously messy plate of rice flooded with curry and braised gravy, piled with crispy pork chop, chap chye and braised egg. The collision of sauces is the whole point, and it is magnificent.
stall: Loo's Hainanese Curry Rice, Redhill Food Centre

name: Avocado Juice
description: Ripe avocado blended thick and velvety with milk and a ribbon of gula melaka down the glass. Rich, buttery-smooth and dessert-like, it commands nightly queues at this famous juice stall.
stall: MJ Avocado Exotic Juices, ABC Brickworks Food Centre

name: Braised Pig Trotter Rice
description: Pig trotters braised low and slow in dark soy, star anise and rock sugar until the skin turns gelatinous and the meat slips off the bone. Served with rice, egg and sharp pickled vegetables.
stall: Ah Bee Pig Trotter Specialist, Alexandra Village Food Centre

name: Steamed Yam Cake
description: Savoury steamed cake dense with taro cubes, dried shrimp and mushrooms, blanketed in fried shallots, spring onion and chilli sauce. Soft, earthy and fragrant, an underrated teatime pleasure.
stall: Traditional Orh Kueh Stall, ABC Brickworks Food Centre

name: Pig Organ Soup
description: A clear, peppery pork broth brimming with liver, intestine, lean meat and salted vegetables, sharpened with a dab of chilli and vinegar dip. Clean-tasting, warming and beloved by generations of purists.
stall: Koh Brothers Pig's Organ Soup, Berseh Food Centre

name: Pan-Fried Dumplings
description: Handmade dumplings crisped golden on the bottom and steamed juicy above, packed with pork and chive filling that gushes savoury juices. Dip in black vinegar and shredded ginger for full effect.
stall: Shandong Dumpling House, Geylang Bahru Market & Food Centre

name: Bubur Cha Cha
description: A warm Nyonya dessert of steamed sweet potato, taro and chewy tapioca jewels swimming in a fragrant pandan-infused coconut cream broth. Creamy, colourful and gently sweet, comfort in a bowl on rainy evenings.
stall: Nyonya Sweets Stall, Berseh Food Centre

name: Ayam Bakar
